decision: scoped cycle 1 to three arithmetic tasks and six conversation conditions
why: the execution loop must work before repository and verifier transformations earn complexity

decision: made repeat the primary control for evolving conditions
why: static and evolving conversations otherwise differ in both intent changes and model-call count

decision: deferred repository mutation and transformed verifiers from cycle 1
why: four independent reviewers agreed the current symbolic variant layer is disconnected from execution

decision: chose HUD Chat as the multi-turn execution boundary
why: HUD v6 documents persistent message history and one fresh model run per user turn

decision: classified the first smoke run as a harness error instead of model failure
why: HUD Chat requires explicit runtime placement and the runner omitted it
result: fixed with LocalRuntime and retained failed row

decision: rejected Haiku as the cycle 1 measurement model
why: static accuracy was 2 of 6, too low to attribute later failures to intent evolution

decision: opened a Sonnet 4.5 campaign with the same tasks and protocol
why: a stronger static ceiling is required before measuring an evolving-intent gap

decision: accepted Sonnet 4.5 and froze the measurement baseline
why: static and four-call repeat controls both scored 6 of 6 with no provider or harness errors

decision: rejected every four-turn intent perturbation as saturated
why: reveal, revision, switch, and combined each scored 6 of 6 against a 6 of 6 matched control
result: no qualitative effect, increase transition depth

decision: fixed the next-intervention selector after saturation
why: it incorrectly selected a tied condition instead of increasing task depth

decision: rejected the seven-turn combined perturbation as saturated
why: combined-deep and repeat-deep each scored 6 of 6 under Sonnet 4.5
result: no effect, task-model pair is too easy

decision: opened a GPT 5.6 Luna calibration campaign
why: Haiku lacked static competence while Sonnet saturated every perturbation; an intermediate model may expose the boundary

decision: rejected the GPT Luna multi-turn campaign as a HUD harness incompatibility
why: all six static calls passed, but every later Chat turn failed OpenAI Responses message validation
result: 12 harness errors excluded from model metrics

decision: opened an easier Haiku campaign with the seven-turn protocol
why: Haiku needs a higher static ceiling while retaining lower intent-tracking capacity

decision: rejected the easier Haiku campaign as saturated
why: static, repeat-deep, and combined-deep each scored 6 of 6

decision: opened a boundary campaign around the only original task Haiku solved consistently
why: this preserves static competence while increasing arithmetic and stale-value pressure
result: open until four static repetitions pass

decision: rejected the boundary campaign after repeated static calibration
why: the earlier 2 of 2 success did not replicate; the new campaign scored 1 of 4

decision: pivoted the source-task domain from arithmetic to exact lookup
why: intent tracking should be measured without arithmetic skill dominating the result
